clue.text: Make an ad-lib? One's better without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the better-making verb sits outside the other piece

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
One's is one (I) plus is ('s), giving IS

explanation.surface: A musing on whether a performer does better off-script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'; 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to perform spontaneously, inventing words as one goes rather than following a script.

clue.text: A short musical overture

parts.note: the opening passage of a piece of music, with short also hinting the word is a shortened form

explanation.surface: A brief opening piece before a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' does double duty: the overture is brief, and the word is a clipped form of a longer one.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped form of 'introduction' names the opening section of a song or performance.

clue.text: Putting in charge

parts.note: reads as appointing someone to lead, but means loading an explosive charge into a gun or mine

explanation.surface: Appointing someone to take command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' suggests command; the charge is gunpowder.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing a firearm or explosive by adding the powder that ignites it is the technical sense.

clue.text: Nothing disturbed bees like being overweight

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: disturbed bees are stirred up, so the letters of bees are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hive of bees stirred up and grown fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like being' is a link; 'Nothing' gives the letter O by its round shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seriously heavier than is healthy is the medical sense of being grossly overweight.

clue.text: One thing you still gain when on a decline

definitions.text: One thing you still gain when on a decline

parts.words: One thing you still gain when on a decline
parts.note: going downhill, a moving body picks up momentum, though decline suggests failing fortunes

explanation.surface: A consolation that something is still won even in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' suggests a fall in fortune, but it is a physical slope down which speed builds.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum, the driving force of a moving body, increases as it rolls down a slope.

clue.text: Judges of knitted ties and cooked meats

indicators.note: knitted ties are worked into new shapes, so the letters of ties are rearranged
cooked meats are altered, so the letters of meats are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone assessing knitted neckwear and cooked meats, like a show judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' turns TIES into ESTI and 'cooked' turns MEATS into MATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge or reckon an approximate value, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Miss having a nap on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the nap comes after Sunday

parts.note: a kip is a British slang word for a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone skips a commitment because they are dozing on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something, such as a class or a meal, is to pass over it or leave it out.

clue.text: Rendered a tune, setting up a Spanish drink

parts.note: to render a song is to perform it, so sang

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up turns the tune upwards so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A singer performs before mixing a Spanish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reverses AIR to RIA beneath SANG.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and sometimes brandy.

clue.text: Chill wine to go with ends of turkey and cold game

parts.note: to ice is to chill
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

indicators.note: ends of here takes the final pair of letters of turkey, its tail end

explanation.surface: Instructions for a Christmas meal: chilled wine with turkey leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: This sport is played on ice, so it is literally a cold game.

clue.text: Start playing up after industrial action

indicators.note: placed after signals that the word up follows the strike in the answer

parts.note: a strike is the classic form of industrial action by workers

explanation.surface: A band resumes playing once a walkout ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A band strikes up a tune when it begins performing; the phrasal verb means to begin music.

clue.text: Well-filled vessel

parts.note: a ship carrying a cargo of oil that came out of an oil well; well-filled seems to mean merely full

explanation.surface: A container brimming over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-filled' reads as 'thoroughly full', but the well is an oil well and the vessel a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil-carrying ship holds crude pumped from wells, so its cargo literally comes from a well.

clue.text: Courteous staff accept it

indicators.note: the staff accepts, i.e. takes inside itself, the word it

parts.note: a staff is a long rod, a pole

explanation.surface: Well-mannered employees take things in good grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous and this answer are synonyms, both meaning showing good manners towards others.

clue.text: Cat given alternative to din after midnight?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
or introduces an alternative
a row is a loud noise or din

explanation.surface: A tomcat yowling noisily in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: once midnight passes, it is the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: The day following today begins at midnight, so whatever comes after midnight belongs to the next day.

clue.text: Get off or put on the line

definitions.meaning: end a phone call, putting the receiver down
hang washing or a coat on a line or peg

explanation.surface: Instructions about telephone lines or washing lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a phone call and pegging washing out are both expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Bluster and rage on car breakdown

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the words rage on car apart and reassembles them

explanation.surface: A driver blustering in fury when the car breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluster is loud, overbearing talk, a show of haughty self-importance.

clue.text: Left sheet listing one's financial assets

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a folio is a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A sheet left behind that lists someone's wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor's holdings of shares and bonds are collectively known by this term.

clue.text: Delays defeats

explanation.surface: A list of a campaign's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse in progress can be either a hold-up or an outright loss, and both senses share one plural noun.

clue.text: Neat island type of boat

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy
Aran is an island (or island group) off the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A tidy island craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel with three hulls side by side is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Low gear involved, finding place to park?

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of gear are tangled up

explanation.surface: A driver in low gear looking for a parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low gear' reads as a car's first gear; 'involved' makes RAGE from GEAR. The query flags that boats, not cars, park here.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth where a vessel is tied up is a place to park a boat.

clue.text: Just come in, unplaced

parts.note: just, as in 'just now', means at this moment
something that has come in has arrived and is here

explanation.surface: A racehorse that has just finished but failed to be placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that finishes out of the top places is said to be nowhere in the race.

clue.text: Stragglers revealed in the street lights

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Latecomers caught under the streetlamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals or people who wander off from the group and lag behind are stragglers.

clue.text: Country has a craze to support rugby union

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a mania is a craze

explanation.surface: A country gripped by enthusiasm for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an older English spelling of the Balkan nation now usually called Romania.

clue.text: Not many virtuous? Quite a lot in fact

definitions.meaning: a few good ones, read literally as only a small number of good people
the idiom means a fair number

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark that there are few good people, then a correction.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom literally says 'a few' yet means a considerable number, which the clue's 'in fact' plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a considerable number, despite containing a word for a small quantity.

clue.text: Just short of a Left majority

parts.note: most means the greater part, the majority

explanation.surface: A left-wing party falls just short of a majority in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly reaching but not quite reaching a mark means falling just short of it.

clue.text: Given such a start, where you should be

definitions.text: Given such a start, where you should be

parts.words: Given such a start, where you should be
parts.note: a start of the sort that puts you in front before the race begins; being given it, you should be leading

explanation.surface: Advice to someone given an early advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The kind of start meant is 'a head start'; given one, you should be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front, in the lead, is where a head start should put you.

clue.text: Enemy the Salvation Army has to beat

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army must defeat its foe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is the Enemy, a traditional biblical title for the adversary of God.

clue.text: Necessitate being in late, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of in late could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something forces a person to arrive late.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN LATE are rearranged; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve something as a necessary consequence, so it means to necessitate.

clue.text: No end of time

parts.note: time without any ending, endless duration; it reads like 'a great deal of time'

explanation.surface: A complaint about a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' usually means plenty, but here it means time that literally never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinite, unending time is exactly what this word denotes.

clue.text: Present her with a key

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Handing a woman a key as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a verb meaning give, but it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone present is in attendance, the word answered at a roll call.

clue.text: So greatly tempted, got into debt

parts.note: over as a prefix means excessively, to so great a degree
drawn means attracted or tempted

explanation.surface: Someone yields to temptation and spends beyond their means.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account in deficit has had more withdrawn than it contained, so its owner owes money.
